citation.title: Sketch2Topo: Diffusion-Model-Based Topology Optimization Using Hand-Drawn Inputs as Condition Constraints
citation.authors: Shuyue Feng, Cedric Caremel, Yoshihiro Kawahara
citation.venue: CHI EA '26: Extended Abstracts of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, Article 599, pp. 1-5 (poster); also arXiv preprint (cs.HC)
citation.version_coded: Version of record (ACM DL full-text HTML, CC BY 4.0, published 13 Apr 2026), read in full in the in-app browser on 2026-09-24; cross-checked against arXiv v1 (19 Mar 2026; only version) HTML: same text and same Table 1. The arXiv title differs (see notes).

included.reason: I-QUALITY (screened I-UNCLEAR; the only quantitative classical comparison is on design quality)

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: On a single load case with a 0.2 volume-fraction target, Sketch2Topo's three generation modes (10 samples each) gave higher mean compliance than the SIMP result (67.96-96.49 vs 63.40) and overshot the volume target (21.90-26.34% vs 20%).
claim.key_phrase: the structures generated by Sketch2Topo exhibit higher minimum compliance
claim.location: Section 4.1, Table 1 (first quantitative classical comparison; abstract, introduction and conclusion hold none)
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: No runtime of any method is reported anywhere in the article. The speed argument is only motivation: the abstract says classical TO has significant computational and time costs, and Section 1 says classical runs can take hours (citing Aage et al. 2017). Not derivable.
claim.alternatives: (1) Abstract, qualitative motivation: classical TO is costly in computation and time; no Sketch2Topo timing is given. (2) Introduction, qualitative: sketching is said to speed up the engineering workflow and to improve aesthetics compared with traditional methods; neither is measured. (3) Table 1 per mode vs SIMP (63.40; 20%): image-to-image 94.97 ± 30.64 and 21.90 ± 0.67%; mask 1 96.49 ± 48.77 and 24.76 ± 1.49%; mask 2 67.96 ± 18.71 and 26.34 ± 1.55% [derived: mean compliance +49.8%, +52.2%, +7.2%]. The authors call the compliance increase acceptable and inevitable.

baseline.classical_method: SIMP compliance minimization: the FEA group in Table 1, which the Fig. 1a caption describes as SIMP-based finite element analysis; vertical load at (0.98, 0.96), supports at (0.26, 0.0) and (0.0, 0.62), volume fraction 0.2 (Section 4.1)
baseline.problem_size: not stated (coordinates are given in normalized units, Section 4.1)
baseline.training_time: none for this work: the pretrained open-source TopoDiff model is used without retraining or fine-tuning (Sections 3.1-3.2); TopoDiff's own training cost not stated
baseline.data_generation_cost: none for this work; the base model's training-data cost is not stated
baseline.quality_metric: minimum compliance and volume fraction of the generated designs, mean ± std over 10 generations per mode (Table 1); the evaluator for generated designs is not described [FE with the listed SIMP parameters inferred: r_min = 2.0, p = 3.0, ν = 0.3, E0 = 1, Emin = 10⁻⁹, Section 4.1]
baseline.quality_gap: Compliance: SIMP 63.40 vs 94.97 ± 30.64 (image-to-image), 96.49 ± 48.77 (mask 1), 67.96 ± 18.71 (mask 2) [derived: +49.8%, +52.2%, +7.2% of the means]. Volume fraction: 20% (SIMP, target 0.2) vs 21.90 ± 0.67%, 24.76 ± 1.49%, 26.34 ± 1.55% (Table 1)

R1.evidence: Section 4.1, Table 1: all groups share the load case, material, penalty and filter settings and a 0.2 volume target, so the comparison is on design quality only. Volume is not matched: Sketch2Topo outputs hold 21.90-26.34% material vs 20% for SIMP, which favours their compliance [inferred]. The design domains probably differ too [inferred]: the authors attribute the compliance gap to regional constraints imposed by the sketches. Ten generations per mode are compared with one SIMP run; the SIMP stopping rule and any compute budget are not stated.

R2.evidence: Sections 3.2 and 4.1: the SIMP settings are given (r_min = 2.0, p = 3.0, ν = 0.3, E0 = 1, Emin = 10⁻⁹, volume fraction 0.2), but the implementation, solver, iteration count and stopping rule are not. SIMP gives the lowest compliance in Table 1 (63.40), so nothing indicates an under-converged comparator [inferred]. No runtimes exist, so markers (a)-(e) cannot apply. Unsure → pass.

R3.evidence: No speed claim: no runtime of any method is reported. For C3: the pretrained TopoDiff model is used without retraining or fine-tuning (Sections 3.1-3.2); its data-generation and training costs are not reported in this article.

R4.evidence: Table 1: compliance and volume fraction are reported as mean ± std over all 10 generations per mode, and the volume overshoot is disclosed (Section 4.1). How the compliance of the generated designs was computed is not stated [FE with the listed SIMP parameters inferred]. Disconnected, floating-material or otherwise failed generations are not counted.

reporting.n_test_cases: 1 load case: 3 Sketch2Topo modes × 10 generations each vs 1 SIMP run (Table 1); plus a qualitative chair study with 10 and 20 generations and 3 mask variants (Section 4.2)

notes: Coded the version of record (CHI EA '26, Article 599, CC BY 4.0), whose text and Table 1 match arXiv v1; the arXiv v1 and pool title is 'Sketch2Topo: Using Hand-Drawn Inputs for Diffusion-Based Topology Optimization'. The ACM PDF and HTML returned HTTP 403 to scripted access; the in-app browser loaded the full HTML. Type judgment call: a 5-page CHI poster extended abstract with methods and results, treated as a conference paper, not an abstracts-only record (PROTOCOL §3.3, §4). Stratum: screening code was I-UNCLEAR; the full text has no runtime for any method, and the only quantitative classical comparison (Table 1) concerns quality, so stratum Q. Direction 'underperform' because every Sketch2Topo mode has higher mean compliance and more material than SIMP; the authors call the gap acceptable. The article's advantages are usability and aesthetics, which lie outside R1-R4 (PROTOCOL §10). OOD 'unclear': sketched non-square domains differ from the square domains the base model was trained on [inferred], but no test is labelled out-of-distribution. Variance = Table 1 (mean ± std over 10 generations). The chair study (Section 4.2) shows only the most dissimilar outputs, a selection rule the authors state, uses designer votes, and has no classical comparison. No code or data statement for Sketch2Topo; the base model TopoDiff is open source. retest_candidate false: no speed claim and no Sketch2Topo code.
